**[00:00:00]** What you're looking at right over here is a page from my lab notebook. Every page has a date at the top, a question in the first line, and nothing torn out, ever. So today I want to show you how I keep one, and why I think the habit matters more than any tool you could buy for it. The first thing is the question. Before I touch anything I write down what I expect to happen and why. It takes thirty seconds, and it is the line I read first when I come back to the page a month later. The second thing is the result, written as it happens, with the time beside it, even when it is boring. Especially when it is boring, because the boring runs are the ones you forget you did.

**[00:00:51]** The third thing is the link. When a page builds on an older one, I write the older page number in the margin, and over a year those numbers turn the notebook into a map of how I actually think. That map is the whole point. A notebook you can follow backwards is worth ten notebooks you can only read forwards, and it costs nothing but the habit of writing one number down.
